html:
The Piscataway were an Algonquian-speaking people of the north bank of the Potomac River in southern Maryland, around Piscataway Creek. Their paramount chief, the tayac, led a group of tribes on the Maryland side of the river, while the Patawomeck and others lived across it in Virginia. Their neighbours upstream included the Nacotchtank.

When English Catholics founded the Province of Maryland in 1634, the Piscataway welcomed them as allies against raids by the Susquehannock. The Jesuit Andrew White baptised the tayac Kittamaquund in 1640. As settlers took their land, most Piscataway moved north in the early 1700s, to Pennsylvania and later New York, where they lived under the protection of the Iroquois and were known as the Conoy. Families who stayed in Maryland kept a quiet identity, and the state recognised two Piscataway groups in 2012.
